transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because I've been dealing with these worries that I just can't seem to control. Once a worry starts—whether it's about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or just worrying that I missed something at work—I just can't seem to shelve it in my mind. 

I try, you know, I make lists, or I try really hard to redirect my focus to something else, but it doesn't work. The worry just stays there and I can't put it away.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes, it's definitely not just one thing. Over this past year, it feels like it's just spread to everything. It started out mainly with worrying about my mother's safety, but now it's... well, it's finances, it's staff decisions at the library, deadlines, things around the house. I even worry constantly about whether I'm being a good daughter. It just feels like even the small things can start to feel like they're about to unravel.
When these worries come up, do you feel driven to do certain repeated behaviors or mental rituals to make the anxiety go down?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I make my lists to try and stay organized, but I don't feel like I have to do certain things over and over just to feel better. It's really just the worrying itself that I can't stop.
Did these worries begin after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Yes, it did. Um, this has been going on for about a year and two months now. It started right after my mother had a fall and had to move into my home. That was a pretty big change, and that's really when all of this began.
Do these worries feel out of proportion to what is actually happening?

I'm not entirely sure. To me, they feel like real problems. I mean, my mother really did fall, and there are actual issues at the library. So the things I'm stressing over are real. I guess... maybe the amount of time I spend worrying about them is what's out of proportion, but the concerns themselves feel pretty justified to me.
If your mother had never fallen and moved into your home, do you think these worries would still have become this intense?

I really don't know. Um, it's hard to say. Things were definitely more manageable before she moved in, so... maybe not? But I honestly just don't know if it would have gotten this intense anyway. I just know that right now, it's a lot to handle.
Has this level of worrying continued for more than six months since your mother moved into your home?
Yes, it definitely has. Um, like I mentioned a little bit ago, it's been about a year and two months now since she moved in after her fall. So, yes, it's been well over six months.
Right now, does your worrying extend well beyond your mother’s situation into many other parts of your life?

Yes, it definitely does. Over this past year, it’s really spread from just my mother’s safety to... well, a lot of other things. I worry about our finances, staff decisions at the library, deadlines, the house... even just whether I’m being a good daughter to her. It’s gotten to the point where, um, even small things can start to feel like they’re about to completely unravel.
Have you been feeling keyed up or on edge a lot of the time?

Um, I don't think so. I mean, I'm definitely stressed and overwhelmed by all the things I have to think about, but... no, I wouldn't really say I feel keyed up or on edge. I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, definitely. Most nights, I just lie there replaying everything that happened during the day and trying to plan for every possible problem that could come up. And then, if I do manage to fall asleep, the slightest noise wakes me up. If I hear my mother moving around in her room, I’m instantly awake, and it usually takes me an hour or two to get back to sleep. By the time I have to get up and go to the library, I feel like I haven't really rested at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from the lack of sleep and just... stressed out from all the worrying. But I don't really feel down or hopeless. Just very overwhelmed by everything I have to manage.
Has this worrying been interfering with how well you function day to day?

Yes, I think it has. At work—at the library—I've started missing small but important details. And recently, I actually had to hand off parts of a grant presentation because I just... froze up. That's really not like me at all. It's honestly made me worry about whether I can keep leading my team well.
When you start worrying, do you find it hard to stop or control the worrying?

Yes, it is. Actually, that's really why I came in to see you. Once a worry starts—whether it's about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or just whether I missed something at work—I can’t seem to shelve it in my mind. I try to. I make lists, or I try really hard to redirect myself to another task, but... no matter what I do, I just can't seem to stop the thoughts once they get going.
Do you feel that the amount of time and energy you spend worrying is more than the situation actually calls for?

Yes, I think it is. I mean, over this past year, the worrying has really spread. It used to just be about my mother’s safety, which makes sense, but now it’s... it's everything. I spend so much time worrying about finances, staff decisions at the library, deadlines, the house... even just whether I’m being a good daughter. It feels like even really small things can start to feel like they’re just about to unravel completely. So, yes, it's definitely way more energy than these situations actually call for.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes, definitely. During cataloging reviews or even staff meetings, I’ll be looking right at the screen or the agenda, and then I'll suddenly realize I haven’t absorbed a single word. My mind just wanders off into some problem I feel like I should have prevented, and I completely lose focus on what's right in front of me.
Have you been having a lot of muscle tension?

Yes, quite a bit. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders just feel completely locked up. I think I'm just constantly bracing myself. And I've noticed I catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, too... like when I'm answering emails at work, or even just sitting at home listening to see if my mother is moving around in the next room. It's just this constant tightness.
